evidence: src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: `execute(state: any)` accepts untyped raw input instead of a typed `OrderStateType` request.

src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: `if (Array.isArray(state)) { stateStr = state[0]?.toString() || ''; } else if (typeof state === 'string') {...}` cleans up the HTTP query parameter (`string | string[]`), which is transport work for the infrastructure layer.
src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: `this.orderRepository.findByState(stateStr as OrderStateType)` casts the parsed string without checking it against the domain states.
Graph: OrderController (infrastructure) injects ListOrdersByStateUseCase, so request parsing should happen in that controller.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This is an application use case, so it should run the use case against a typed input and map results into an application DTO. Mapping to the DTO in `mapToResponse` is fine here. The problem is in `execute(state: any)`. It accepts an untyped value, checks `Array.isArray(state)`, takes `state[0]?.toString()`, and otherwise falls back to a string check. That is how you clean up a raw HTTP query parameter, which in Express can be a `string` or a `string[]`. The graph shows `OrderController` in infrastructure injects this use case, so that cleanup belongs in the controller (infrastructure/transport). The controller should pass a typed `OrderStateType`. The use case also never checks the string against the valid domain states. It just casts it with `stateStr as OrderStateType`, so this transport handling replaces proper validation of the input.
